transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I guess… I’ve been having trouble finishing things I mean to follow up on. After audits or mentorship events, I’ll start the final email or a review note or some form, and I really intend to finish it. Then a few days later I realize it never actually got done. That’s what pushed me to make the appointment.
Do you often have trouble staying focused on tasks in other parts of your life too, not just at work?

Yes… I think so. It happens in meetings or trainings too. I’ll start out paying attention, like in a long client meeting or an AI-tool training, and then at some point I realize I’ve sort of drifted off and missed the last few minutes, even though I’m still looking at the screen.
When you were a child, did you also often have trouble paying attention or finishing tasks?

Yes… I think so. My report cards were always kind of the same—“bright,” but I’d lose assignments or rush through and miss little details. I needed reminders to finish things.

My mom still brings up that I could do well on a test but somehow forget the project sitting in my backpack.
Do you often feel restless, like it’s hard to sit still?

Yes. Mostly during long reviews or meetings. Sitting still starts to feel… uncomfortable, like pressure building up. I’ll end up standing, walking to the printer, or finding some excuse to move around.
Do these attention problems also cause difficulties for you at home?

Yes. I don’t love admitting that, but… at home my husband has taken over some of the bills and things I said I’d handle, because I don’t always follow through reliably.

It’s caused tension. And at work it’s been showing too—mistakes and unfinished follow-up got bad enough to affect a client review, and now I worry people are wondering if I can really handle the promotion.
Outside of work, do you also often have trouble staying organized and following through on everyday tasks?

Yes. It’s… mostly the follow-through. I’ll start something after an audit or a mentorship event, fully meaning to finish it, and then a few days later I realize the final email or review note or some form just never got done. That’s actually part of what made me make this appointment.
Do these problems with attention and follow-through happen in more than one setting, not just at work?

Yes… it’s not just work.

At work it’s gotten noticeable — mistakes, things I didn’t follow up on, and it affected a client review. I’ve been worried people are questioning whether I can handle the promotion.

And at home… my husband has had to take over some bills and commitments I said I’d handle, because he can’t really count on me to finish them reliably.
Do you often feel anxious or worried, even when there isn’t an immediate problem in front of you?
I’m not sure. I mean… I worry when there’s something specific going on, but I don’t know that it’s just there all the time for no reason.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
I don’t think depressed, exactly. Maybe frustrated or tired of dealing with this, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling down most of the time.
